items.name: Kisspeptin
items.benefits: Investigational benefits depend on the peptide variant and clinical setting. Kisspeptin-54 induced egg maturation in women receiving IVF, and a randomized study in women at high risk of ovarian hyperstimulation found improved mature-oocyte yield with a second administration. Small acute kisspeptin-54 studies also reported changes in sexual brain processing and arousal in people with low sexual desire. These findings do not establish routine fertility or libido treatment with an unspecified kisspeptin product.

source_statements.section: Who Kisspeptin Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Human kisspeptin research has focused on healthy adult men, premenopausal women, women with missing periods from low hormone signaling, IVF trigger studies, and men and women with low sexual desire disorder. Outside those research settings, evidence is still limited.

source_statements.section: Who Kisspeptin Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Pregnancy and lactation: Kisspeptin is tied to pregnancy and reproductive cycling. There is no good safety data for use during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

source_statements.section: Who Kisspeptin Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Hormone-sensitive cancers: Kisspeptin can affect sex-hormone signaling. That matters for breast, ovarian, or prostate cancer history.

source_statements.section: Who Kisspeptin Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Active fertility treatment outside a clinical trial: Do not try to copy an IVF trigger protocol without clinical monitoring. Timing, labs, and ultrasound checks matter.

source_statements.section: Who Kisspeptin Is For and Who Should Avoid It
source_statements.excerpt: Pediatric or adolescent use: Kisspeptin is part of puberty timing. It should not be used casually in children or teens.

In published human studies, kisspeptin-10 and kisspeptin-54 were generally well tolerated when used short term. The low-desire studies reported no treatment-related serious adverse events. IVF trigger studies reported minor events, but no severe drug-related events clearly tied to kisspeptin-54.
Disruption of normal GnRH pulse timing. GnRH is the brain signal that starts LH and FSH release.
